title: Establish Companion IssueStack and proposal authority
evidence_required: Governance-aggregate migration/model results with native UUID/FK/check/partial-unique plus advanced Safety Gate, Task Follow-Up, and all older exact-head regression evidence.
Boss, granted Engineer, Consultant read-only, current grant, wrong-Farm, archive, restore, and no-existence-leak matrix evidence.

IssueStack ordering/focus, active-attention reuse, proposal sequence/supersede, request fingerprint, same-run identical retry/conflict, distinct-run serialized multi-effect behavior, and controlled concurrent-write evidence.
Attention/proposal UI identity, literal redaction, Timeline cardinality, retained feed read, and projection-conflict rollback evidence.

Exact issue/detail HTTP fields, canonical refs, active-else-latest attention, proposal ordering/nullability, no-store/error behavior, and proof that this wave exposes no run, decision, close, Task, Bus, Safety, Plant-state, or device authority.
purpose: Establish the retained PostgreSQL governance aggregate and independently verifiable IssueStack/current-proposal authority that later human-decision and real-Companion waves can consume without duplicating focus, attention, supersede, projection, or idempotency logic.
success_outcome: The backend can persist and read one Plant-scoped IssueStack with at most one focused open issue, one active HumanAttentionNeeded cycle, and one current pending proposal per issue; a newer validated proposal atomically supersedes the previous pending proposal while reusing active attention, exact retries are idempotent, conflicts/archive/grant races write nothing, and only strict non-agent-consumable attention/proposal UI plus redacted issue/proposal Timeline records are emitted, with no public mutation or binding decision/effect path yet.
anti_goals: Do not expose the explicit model run, proposal decision, issue close, or arbitrary proposal-create HTTP command in this wave.
Do not register the Companion router in backend/app/main.py; TASK-043 owns the single production registration after TASK-040, while this wave verifies its read routes through an isolated test app.
Do not implement DecisionRecord transitions, ordinary-task effects, DecisionRecord Bus/context publication, or real provider invocation; TASK-042 and TASK-043 own those outcomes.
Do not add a governance permission, reuse plant_approve_actions, forbid self-approval, add Farm-level issues, expiry, reopen, hard delete, or persist CompanionConclusion.
Do not add frontend/PWA, scheduler, worker, outbox, raw proposal Bus publication, Timeline replay authority, or physical-action/Plant/device semantics.

forbidden_scope: TASK-042 DecisionRecord/close commands, ordinary-task source/effects, decision Bus/context, or binding decision projections.
TASK-043 Companion request/result, provider composition, external egress, explicit run endpoint, or credentialed smoke.
New permission flags, plant_approve_actions governance semantics, self-approval restrictions, or Farm-level governance.
Safety approval, action Task, Plant-state confirmation, device commands, automated actuation, frontend/PWA, scheduler, worker, outbox, or hard delete.
stop_conditions: The actual TASK-039 migration head or persisted classification/shared UI constraints differ materially from the linked canonical contracts.
The four-table governance aggregate cannot preserve exact restrictive/deferrable relations and terminal DecisionRecord references in one additive schema revision.
Focus, active-attention reuse, proposal supersede, required UI projections, and Timeline refs cannot commit atomically under concurrent writes.
Implementation would require a public proposal mutation, raw proposal/rationale as agent fact, a new permission, or Timeline/UI replay as mutable authority.
Existing uncommitted work makes the aggregate migration or shared Agent Chat/API/writer edits unsafe to reconcile.

constraints: The first FT-013 migration creates the complete four-table governance aggregate so proposal/attention terminal references are never weakened, but this wave creates no DecisionRecord row or decision command.
Every exact-head assertion present after TASK-039, including Safety Gate and Task Follow-Up migration-model tests, advances to the aggregate revision in this task.
The Companion read router is verified through an isolated FastAPI test app and is not registered in backend/app/main.py until TASK-043 serializes production composition after TASK-040.
Proposal persistence accepts only a validated matching classification/runtime handoff through the internal service; no public caller may submit proposal text, effect, refs, or authorization data.

One Plant has at most one focused open issue; one issue has at most one active attention and pending proposal; a newer proposal supersedes the current pending proposal and reuses active attention atomically.
Boss and granted Engineer use existing current can_operate authority for internal proposal persistence; Consultant has authorized reads only, and archive blocks every write with no restore replay.

Attention/proposal UI projections use authoritative ids, remain non-agent-consumable, and proposal state updates preserve original identity/timestamp; issue/proposal Timeline payloads are redacted correlation summaries.

CompanionConclusion is derived from retained authority and reports awaiting_human for an active/current pair whether its open issue is focused or unfocused; it is never persisted or emitted as a separate event.

FT-013 refs use exactly companion_issue, companion_attention, companion_proposal, and decision_record kinds; proposal source refs are provider input refs followed by message_envelope and safety_classification refs, with no aliases or caller additions.

Same-run concurrency commits one effect; different run ids are independent explicit commands and may both commit in governance lock order, with the later existing-issue writer superseding or the later new-issue writer becoming sole focus.
invariants: PostgreSQL is IssueStack, attention, and proposal authority; Timeline, UI Feed, MessageEnvelope, classification, and derived conclusion cannot independently create, repair, replay, or transition records.

Proposal/rationale/provider result content and UI projections are not published to Agent Chat Bus by this wave; later agent-specific provider input is governed by its own strict typed allowlist and remains non-authoritative.
No public run/decision/close, Task, Safety/action, Plant-state, completion, Outcome, or device authority exists in this wave.
Archive retains governance rows and authorized reads but blocks focus/proposal persistence; restore never replays denied work.
Identical run source/fingerprint returns the first canonical proposal; stale versions, conflicting identity reuse, uniqueness races, and projection conflicts write nothing.
verification_targets: Migration/model tests prove all four governance tables, native UUID/FK/enums/checks, restrictive/deferrable relations, partial uniqueness, request fingerprints, actual post-FT-012 head, and advanced Safety Gate, Task Follow-Up, and older exact-head assertions.

PostgreSQL read/write and concurrency tests prove IssueStack ordering, one focus, active-else-latest attention, proposal sequence/supersede, same-run duplicate versus conflict, distinct-run serialized supersede/refocus, readable open/unfocused awaiting_human detail, exact canonical source refs, and archive/grant races.

Projection tests prove exact attention/proposal UI identities and terminal update idempotency, literal/redacted payloads, issue/proposal Timeline cardinality, rollback on projection/audit failure, and unchanged FT-008 variants.

Isolated-router HTTP/OpenAPI tests prove exact issue list/detail fields, refs, attention selection, proposal ordering/nullability, exact status-rank cursor ordering, no-store, total applicable errors, no-existence leak, retained archive history, Consultant read access, and absence of run/decision/close mutations without touching production main.py.
Static/effect spies prove no DecisionRecord row, ordinary/action Task, Bus event, Safety approval, Plant mutation, provider call, or device effect is possible from this wave.
